report.source_text: Histological analysis showed proliferation of the chorion in the form of small nests with relatively uniform, medium-sized cells and rounded to polyhedral cells containing homogenous, ovoid nuclei with fine chromatin. It was associated with numerous thin-walled vascular structures, lined by endothelial cells without atypia. The tumour cells containing a cytoplasmic frame well defined by reticulin were positive for actin and caldesmone with low expression for CD99. There was no expression for pancytokeratins, CD34, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100 protein, SOX-10, desmin or inhibin. There also was no signs of malignancy.

report.source_text: Emergency upper airway stabilisation and haemostasis were immediately performed in the operating room. The initial endoscopic examination showed an active and significant bleed emerging from a large tumour in the trachea. The patient was therefore intubated with a size five endotracheal tube to insure ventilation. Taking into account the seriousness of the situation allows surgical tracheotomy between the third and fourth tracheal rings given the location and the lack of knowledge as to the extent of the tumour. A non-fenestrated cuffed tracheal cannula was then introduced.

report.source_text: The patient underwent volumetric intensity by arc therapy radiation at a total dose of 53 Gy over 25 sessions, with a frequency of five sessions per week. He was kept hospitalised during this period. The treatment was well tolerated without side effects or complications. He remained stable without either recurrence of bleeding or respiratory distress.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An elderly man presented with acute respiratory distress and massive haemoptysis, preceded by self-resolving episodes of bloody sputum. Initial endoscopic examination revealed a large, actively bleeding tracheal tumor causing significant obstruction (90% of lumen). Emergency intubation and surgical tracheotomy were performed for airway stabilization. A CT scan further characterized the 25mm posterior parietal tracheal mass with contrast uptake and local infiltration. Biopsies of the tracheal mass were taken, and histological analysis showed proliferation of chorion in small nests, medium-sized cells, numerous thin-walled vascular structures, positive staining for actin and caldesmone, low CD99 expression, and negativity for other markers, consistent with glomangioma subtype of glomus tumor. The patient received volumetric intensity by arc therapy radiation (53 Gy over 25 sessions), which was well tolerated, resulting in a stable condition without recurrence of bleeding or respiratory distress.
